title: Local weather patterns
keyIdea: A weather pattern is weather that happens again and again where you live. To find one, observe the weather at the same time each day and record it in a weather diary: sunny, cloudy, rainy, windy, warm or cold. Then count the days. The weather with the most days is the pattern for that week, even if one day stands out in your memory. A thermometer shows that the afternoon is usually warmer than the early morning, because the sun warms the air through the day. Over a year, places with four seasons have colder, shorter days in winter and warmer, longer days in summer. One day on its own is not a pattern.
familyTip: Make a weather diary on the fridge for two weeks. At breakfast, look out of the window together and draw the weather in that day's box. On Friday, count: how many rainy days, how many sunny? If you have a thermometer, read it before school and after school and see which is warmer.

visual.caption: Is it a weather pattern or just one day? Drag each card into a box, or tap it and then a box.

items: Most days this week were rainy
Afternoons are usually warmer than mornings

lab.caption: Flagship lab: keep a weather diary, count the days in a chart, compare 9 am and 2 pm thermometers, and sort patterns and seasons.

kid: Look out of the window at the same time each day. Is it sunny, cloudy or rainy? Draw it in a weather diary. Do it every day.
At the end of the week, count the days. Rainy, sunny, rainy, cloudy, rainy is 3 rainy days. So this week was mostly rainy. The sunny day may be the one you remember. But counting tells the truth.
A thermometer tells us how warm the air is. In the morning the red line is short. In the afternoon it is taller. The sun warms the air all day. So the afternoon is usually warmer.
A pattern is what happens again and again. 'It snowed on my birthday' is just one day. In places with four seasons, winter days are usually cold and short. Summer days are usually warm and long.
adult: Ages 5 to 6. NGSS K-ESS2-1 asks children to use and share observations of local weather to describe patterns over time. That means sunny, cloudy, rainy and warm days, how many sunny or rainy days come in a month, and that it is usually cooler in the morning than in the afternoon. In England, Year 1 Seasonal changes asks children to describe the weather in each season and how day length changes. Key words: weather, observe, record, weather diary, tally, pattern, temperature, thermometer, season.

Scientists find patterns the same way. They record the same thing at the same time, day after day, and then count. A child's weather diary works like a weather station's record. The afternoon is usually warmest because the sun keeps heating the ground after midday, and the ground warms the air. So the top temperature often comes in mid-afternoon. In the UK and other places with four seasons, winter is colder and darker and summer is warmer and lighter. Near the equator there may be wet and dry seasons instead.

Common mistakes: naming the week from the one day that stood out, such as a sunny sports day in a rainy week; thinking the early morning is the warmest time; calling one event a pattern; thinking a pattern must happen every time, so one rainy day 'breaks' a mostly sunny week; and expecting the same weather in every season. Weather is what happens on one day. A pattern needs many days of records.

In the lab children record five days from window views. They move each day into a Sunny, Cloudy or Rainy block chart and count. They compare a 9 am and a 2 pm thermometer for five days. Then they sort sentences into 'a pattern' or 'just one day', and sort weather cards into winter or summer.

practice.prompt: Local weather patterns: a diary says rain, sun, rain, cloud, rain. What was this week's pattern?
practice.hint: Count each kind of weather. Which one has the most days?
practice.explain: Rain 3 days, sun 1 day, cloud 1 day. Rain has the most days, so the week was mostly rainy.

practice.prompt: A weather diary has {r} rainy days and {s} sunny days. How many days are in the diary?
practice.hint: Count all the rainy days and all the sunny days together.
practice.explain: {r} rainy days and {s} sunny days make {=r+s} days in the diary.

practice.prompt: When is the air usually warmer?
choices: It is the same all day
practice.hint: Think about the thermometer's red line in the morning and after lunch.
practice.explain: The sun warms the air all through the day, so the afternoon is usually warmer than the early morning.

practice.prompt: In a week of 7 days, {r} days were rainy. How many days were not rainy?
practice.hint: Start with 7 days and take away the rainy days.
practice.explain: 7 days take away {r} rainy days leaves {=7-r} days that were not rainy.

practice.prompt: Which one is a weather pattern?
choices: Most days in July were warm
My hat blew off on Friday
practice.hint: A pattern happens again and again, on lots of days.
practice.explain: 'Most days in July were warm' is about many days, so it is a pattern. The others are about one day.

pool.prompt: Why do we look at the weather at the same time each day?
choices: So the days are fair to compare
pool.hint: Morning and afternoon can be different. How do you make days fair to compare?
pool.explain: If you always look at the same time, the days are fair to compare. Looking can never change the weather.

pool.prompt: Sam's week was rain, rain, sun, rain, rain. He remembers the sunny day best. Was the week mostly sunny?
choices: Yes, one sunny day is enough
pool.hint: Count the days. Do not go by the day you remember.
pool.explain: 4 rainy days and 1 sunny day. The week was mostly rainy. The day you remember best is not always the most common.

pool.prompt: At 9 am the thermometer says 8 °C. At 2 pm it says 14 °C. When was it warmer?
pool.hint: A bigger number on a thermometer means warmer air.
pool.explain: 14 °C is more than 8 °C, so 2 pm was warmer. The red line was taller in the afternoon.

pool.prompt: A class saw {s} sunny days and {c} cloudy days. How many more sunny days than cloudy days?
pool.hint: Take the smaller number away from the bigger number.
pool.explain: {s} sunny days take away {c} cloudy days is {=s-c}, so there were {=s-c} more sunny days.

pool.prompt: Where there are four seasons, which season usually has frost and snow?
pool.hint: Frost and snow need freezing cold air.
pool.explain: Winter is the coldest season, with short days, so frost and snow come in winter.

pool.prompt: Mia says: 'It rained on Monday, so it always rains here.' What is wrong?
choices: One day is not a pattern
pool.hint: How many days did Mia look at?
pool.explain: Mia looked at one day. A pattern needs many days of records that you count.

pool.prompt: In summer, where there are four seasons, the days are usually...
pool.hint: Think of summer evenings. Is it light or dark at bedtime?
pool.explain: Summer days are usually warmer and longer, so it can still be light at bedtime. Winter days are colder and shorter.

pool.prompt: A diary shows {w} windy days each week for 2 weeks. How many windy days is that?
pool.hint: Add the windy days in week 1 and week 2.
pool.explain: {w} windy days in week 1 and {w} in week 2 make {=2*w} windy days.

pool.prompt: Tom saw 4 sunny days and 1 rainy day. Was the week mostly sunny?
choices: No, you need rain to be a pattern
pool.hint: Mostly means on most of the days, not on every day.
pool.explain: 4 of the 5 days were sunny, so the week was mostly sunny. A pattern is what usually happens, not what always happens.
